reference_stocks.name: Corning Incorporated
reference_stocks.theme: Optical fiber as the vital link in AI data-center buildout
reference_stocks.entry_note: Entry at the 2023 year-end close of $30.45, the revenue trough and the quarter Corning launched its Springboard plan off a $13B annualised base. FY2023 revenue fell 11.3% to $12,588M after FY2022's $14,189M, while gross margin held at 33.5% against 34.1% — a 0.6pp give-up on an 11% revenue decline, which is the pricing power of an incumbent nobody can design around. Data-centre enterprise sales then went from $1.3B in 2023 to $3.3B annualised by Q3 2025 on GenAI scale-out. $168.98 as of 2026-09-08, +455% realised from entry.
reference_stocks.why_reference: The vital-link archetype, and the one the screener cannot currently see. At entry Corning failed the quality floor on revenue growth (-11.3%) and sat above every tier ceiling at $26B. It is here to state the intent: a dominant supplier of a component a secular chain physically requires, bought at the trough of its own cycle while the end market inflects — not a hypergrowth small cap.

excluded_reference_stocks.name: MicroVision
excluded_reference_stocks.excluded_reason: Peaked +700% in 2021 on the LiDAR/AV narrative, then fell roughly 95%; the run was a story-stock re-rating, not the durable revenue inflection the other references share. Its pre-run profile also contradicts the screener's own thesis: 12% revenue growth (the lowest of any reference) and 25% three-year dilution (the highest), the exact trait the composite penalises hardest. Because compute_ideal_ranges() uses min/max, MVIS alone set the revenue-growth floor (12%) and the market-cap floor ($150M), widening the 'looks like a winner' band to admit small, slow-growing, heavily diluting companies.
